Action Plan:
1. Right knee pain with clicking during running: continue ice therapy frequently; reduce running volume/intensity and avoid running through pain; take prescribed stronger anti-inflammatory with food; do not take concurrently with ibuprofen; reassess symptoms.
2. Referral to physiotherapy: comprehensive knee assessment arranged; proceed with imaging only if indicated based on physio/clinic exam (to evaluate for possible cartilage/internal derangement).
3. Safety-net advice: seek urgent care if knee develops persistent swelling, heat, redness, fever/feeling unwell, or if the knee locks and you cannot bend/straighten it.
4. Access to care: if physiotherapy wait is prolonged, book in-clinic assessment with our team.
5. Transient right toe tingling post-run: no specific intervention discussed; resolved at time of consult.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Right knee pain and clicking after increasing running; intermittent tingling in right toes after a run.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Onset: ~2 weeks ago.
  - Course: Pain begins ~20 minutes into runs (~mile 2.5–3), worsened on last attempt leading patient to stop. Occasional clicking noted during gym abdominal exercises involving knee flexion/extension. Initial mild swelling after first run improved with ice; currently no swelling and no pain at rest.
  - Location: Primarily right knee; felt centrally, sometimes shifting slightly to the right side of the knee.
  - Laterality: Right knee only (doctor initially referenced both knees; patient clarified right knee).
  - Function: No giving way, locking, or instability. No problems walking, stairs, or range of motion. Able to fully flex and extend the knee.
  - Neurologic symptoms: One episode of tingling in right toes after a run; resolved; no current altered sensation.
  - Vascular symptoms: No color or temperature changes in lower legs; no calf pain. Occasional indentation from socks after prolonged standing reported.
  - Aggravating factors: Running; certain gym movements involving knee flexion/extension.
  - Relieving factors: Ice reduced swelling initially.
- Activity history: Training for a marathon (June). Runs currently 4–8 miles; increased distance began ~1 month ago. Plays multiple sports; prior fall during ice hockey a few months ago resulting in a large bruise (resolved).
- Past medical/surgical history:
  - Farsightedness.
  - LASIK surgery (date not specified).
  - Prior severe UTI; evaluated in ER with concern for kidney stones at the time.
- Medications:
  - Ibuprofen (patient-reported up to 400 mg; route/frequency not documented).
  - “Stronger anti-inflammatory” prescribed today; name/dose/route/frequency not documented; instructed not to combine with ibuprofen and to take with food.
  - Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Aleve (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Xanax for sleep occasionally (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social history:
  - Exercises regularly; marathon training; gym several times per week.
  - Cannabis: “sometimes will smoke a joint.”
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- Consultation type: Video visit; no in-person exam or vitals performed.
- Self-reported musculoskeletal findings:
  - Right knee currently without swelling; full flexion/extension.
  - Pain occurs with running after ~20 minutes; clicking sometimes with flexion/extension during gym movements.
  - No giving way, locking, or stair/walking difficulties.
- Neurologic/vascular (self-reported): One transient episode of right toe tingling post-run; no ongoing numbness/tingling; no color/temperature changes; no calf pain.
- Investigations: None performed today.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Right knee pain with clicking during running:
   - Assessment: Right knee pain; etiology undetermined. Internal derangement (e.g., cartilage injury) not excluded; ACL injury cannot be assessed via video.
   - Investigations planned: Imaging only if indicated after in-person/physiotherapy assessment.
   - Treatment planned: Continue ice therapy; reduce running and avoid running through pain; prescribed a stronger anti-inflammatory to be taken with food; do not take with ibuprofen concurrently.
   - Relevant referrals: Physiotherapy referral for comprehensive assessment and management. Option for clinic evaluation if physiotherapy wait is prolonged.

2. Transient right toe tingling post-run:
   - Assessment: Transient paresthesia of right toes; resolved.
   - Investigations planned: None discussed.
   - Treatment planned: None discussed.

3. Intermittent lower leg sock indentation after prolonged standing:
   - Assessment: Patient-noted indentation; no associated calf pain or color/temperature changes.
   - Investigations planned: None discussed.
   - Treatment planned: None discussed.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergies not recorded; vitals not taken; no detailed medication doses/routes/frequencies for several agents; no detailed knee exam maneuvers possible via video; footwear/orthotics and running surface not discussed.  
● Internal conflicts: Initial reference to “both knees” vs patient clarification that only the right knee hurts (conflict noted). Patient uncertain about the class of “Aleve.”  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor interruptions; no major inaudible segments.
